title: Why a Converted Video Keeps Only One Audio Language (and How to Preserve Both)
primary_question: Why does a converted video lose its second audio language or commentary track, and how can I preserve both without overwriting the source?
source_title: How to Test a Converted Media File Before Replacing the Original

fact_sources.supports: FFmpeg documentation states that with no -map it automatically selects one audio stream based on channel count, then index; using -map controls included streams, and -c copy copies selected streams without transcoding. Chapter mapping is separate: without -map_chapters, chapters are copied from the first input that contains them.
Official ffprobe reference describes -show_entries stream fields and stream_tags fields as well as JSON output for investigating track counts and metadata.
Official formats documentation describes muxers and containers; selecting streams does not override output container support.

new_examples: Fictional bilingual oral-history interview with two-channel English narration and one-channel Korean interpretation: output has one stream; operator explicitly maps both and checks audible language choices.

Fictional student-film archive with two-channel main soundtrack and six-channel director commentary: automatic selection may retain surround commentary; operator maps desired tracks in intended order, checks each, and verifies target player behavior.
